info.name: classifier
info.description:
Document Classifier endpoints — JPEG/PNG, PDF, .txt and .docx uploads scored by OpenCV detectors, deterministic text matching, and vision-LLM criteria — called through the LiteLLM pass-through registered in ai/litellm/litellm_config.yaml (`pass_through_endpoints` → `/v1/classifier` → `http://classifier:8000`, `include_subpath: true`, methods GET/POST/DELETE, `forward_headers: true`). Every request is authenticated with a Bearer token from a LiteLLM virtual key. Set the collection variables `litellm` (e.g. http://localhost:4001) and `virtual master key` (an sk-… key issued from the LiteLLM Admin UI → Virtual Keys) — every request inherits them via collection-level auth. See ai/classifier/API.md for the full endpoint reference and ai/litellm/LITELLM.md for issuing virtual keys.

Direct base URL (bypassing LiteLLM, only useful inside the ai_shared network or when PORT_CLASSIFIER is published): http://classifier:8000 or http://<host>:${PORT_CLASSIFIER}. All examples in this collection use the LiteLLM pass-through path.

Async-job pattern: POST /assess and POST /assess/compare both return 202 Accepted immediately with `{job_id, phase: "pending"}`. Callers poll GET /jobs/{job_id} until `phase` is `completed` or `failed`, then read the `result` field. Concurrency: the SQLite jobs table is the queue — `CLASSIFIER_MAX_CONCURRENT` worker tasks (default 2, `.env`) each atomically claim the oldest `pending` row, so at most that many jobs are analysed at once and pending work survives a container restart (payloads live in `/data/payloads` until the job is terminal). Job tracking is powered by the shared `common.jobs` package (SqliteRegistry backend); the `/jobs`, `/jobs/{id}`, and DELETE `/jobs/{id}` routes are mounted via `common.jobs.router.build_router(..., include_delete=True, include_cancel=False)`. Response migration note: the top-level `id` is now `job_id`, `status` is now `phase`, and the previously separate `type` + `request_id` columns are nested under `metadata`. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}` for the full shape.

Copy the `job_id` from a POST /assess or POST /assess/compare response into the `jobId` collection variable to run the GET/DELETE /jobs/{jobId} requests.

Documents: uploads are not limited to images. `common.documents` detects the kind from the bytes (never the filename or Content-Type) and normalises JPEG/PNG, PDF, plain text, and .docx into pages that may carry an image, a text layer, or both — so `cv` criteria run on page images, `text` criteria search the text layer (OCR-filled for scans and photos), and `llm` criteria see ONE page image plus the extracted text (muse-glimmer runs without `--limit-mm-per-prompt`, so vLLM accepts a single image per request). GET /document-kinds reports the live capability list, and the `Documents` folder in this collection has a ready-to-run request per fixture in unit-tests/classifier/documents/. See API.md § Documents.

Regions and layers: a criterion result can also say WHERE it found something — boxes and polygons in ORIGINAL page pixels — and the job can render those as an SVG overlay, a transparent PNG layer, and a composited JPEG preview, written to a per-job artifact directory served by the four endpoints in the `Artifacts` folder. It is OFF unless a request asks (`regions` on /assess and /assess/compare, implied on /locate): regions cost detector work and layers cost disk. Sources are `cv` (OpenCV detector geometry), `ocr` (recogniser line polygons), `pdf-text` (PyMuPDF rectangles), and `detector` (the open-vocabulary ai/detector service, when DETECTOR_URL is configured). `llm` adds the vision model's own boxes when `regions.llm_boxes` is set — each one asked for on a 0-1000 grid, validated, and verified by cropping it out of the page and asking whether the feature is visible in the crop alone, with EVERY attempt returned. `diff` is change detection on /assess/compare: what appeared, disappeared or changed between the subject and each live example, reported as `aligned: false` with no regions when the two photos are framed too differently to compare. The `Regions` folder mirrors unit-tests/classifier/regions/. See API.md § Regions and layers.

variable.description: LiteLLM base URL. Localhost publish is 4001 (PORT_LITELLM); on ai_shared it's http://litellm:4000; behind cloudflared it's https://your-litellm-host.

LiteLLM virtual key (Admin UI → Virtual Keys, or /key/generate API). Scope the key to allow the /v1/classifier pass-through — most keys created for chat models already do. Sent as `Authorization: Bearer {{virtual master key}}` by the collection-level auth, then forwarded to the classifier by LiteLLM because the pass-through has `forward_headers: true`.

job_id returned by POST /assess, POST /assess/compare, or POST /locate. Fill in after submitting to run GET /jobs/{jobId}, DELETE /jobs/{jobId}, and every request in the Artifacts folder. `phase` values progress staging → pending → processing → completed | failed (`staging` is the few ms before the payload is on disk; workers never claim it).

File name inside a job's artifact directory, used by GET /jobs/{jobId}/artifacts/{artifactName}. Defaults to `regions.json` — the canonical machine-readable layer, keyed by criterion. The others are `manifest.json` (the index, including each criterion's slug), `p{n}.svg` (the overlay), `p{n}.layer.png` (the transparent layer), `p{n}.preview.jpg` (the page with the layer burned in), and `p{n}.base.jpg` (the un-annotated page, present only when the job asked for the preview layer). List them with GET /jobs/{jobId}/artifacts.

Base64 of unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_before.png, WITHOUT a data: prefix. Fill it once: `base64 -w0 unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_before.png` (macOS: `base64 -i ... | tr -d '\n'`; PowerShell: [Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('...'))), then paste the output into this variable's CURRENT VALUE. It is ~150 KB of text, which is why it is a variable rather than being inlined in the request body.

Base64 of unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_after.png, same recipe as scene_before_b64. This is the SUBJECT of the change-detection request — the later photo, with the car that appeared and the shed that went.

request.description: Liveness check used by the Docker healthcheck (`docker-compose.classifier.yml` → `healthcheck.test` hits /health every 30s) and by load balancers. Returns `{"status": "ok"}` with HTTP 200 whenever the FastAPI process is up. Does NOT probe the SQLite jobs registry, the vLLM backend, or the background worker — a stuck worker will still show `status: ok` here. Excluded from Prometheus instrumentation (see `Instrumentator(excluded_handlers=["/metrics", "/health"])` in main.py). See API.md § `GET /health`.

Enumerate all available `hint` values and their LLM scoring rubrics. Returns `{"hints": {"quality": {...}, "presence": {...}, "auto": {...}}}` where each rubric object has `heading`, `rubric`, and `extra` fields sourced from `config.HINT_RUBRICS`. Use these values as the `hint` field on a CriterionInput:

- `quality`: score image quality 1-10 (1-3 = FAIL, 4-6 = MARGINAL, 7-10 = PASS).
- `presence`: detect presence/absence (10=present, 5=uncertain, 1=absent) with chain-of-thought reasoning in `extra`.
- `auto` (default): LLM infers the rubric from the criterion name.

No request body. See API.md § `GET /hints`.

List every registered OpenCV detector, grouped by underlying detector function. Returns `{"detectors": [{"function": "check_blur", "names": ["is blurry", "is sharp", "sharpness"]}, ...], "total_names": N}`. Use any of the `names` as the `name` field on a CriterionInput with `type="cv"` — fuzzy matching is applied at runtime, so near-matches also work. If no detector matches, the criterion silently falls back to LLM scoring and the response's `method` field reflects the actual path taken.

Built-in detector functions: `check_blur` (Laplacian variance), `check_exposure` (mean pixel intensity), `detect_vegetation` (HSV green masking), `detect_sky`, `detect_faces` (Haar cascade), `detect_water`, `detect_text` (Sobel edge density). See API.md § `Built-in cv detector names`.

Note for documents: cv criteria need page images. An image or a PDF has them (PDF pages are rendered at CLASSIFIER_PDF_RENDER_DPI); a .txt or .docx does not, so cv criteria against those come back SKIPPED with `method: "skipped"` and are excluded from the weighted score. On a multi-page document a cv criterion runs on every page and reports the WORST page, with each page's measurement in a `pages` array.

Report what this container accepts as an upload and what it can do with it — cheap introspection, like /hints and /cv-detectors; no job is submitted.

Returns `{kinds, unsupported, text_match_modes, ocr, limits}`:

- `kinds`: one entry per supported kind (`image`, `pdf`, `txt`, `docx`) with its `extensions`, `content_types`, the magic-byte `detection` rule, how many `pages` it can produce, `has_page_images`, `native_text`, and notes. Detection is always by bytes — a PDF uploaded as image/png still loads as a PDF.
- `unsupported`: currently just legacy `.doc` (OLE2, magic `D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1`), rejected with a 400 telling the caller to convert to .docx.
- `text_match_modes`: the four `match` values a `type: "text"` criterion accepts (`contains`, `exact`, `regex` with its 500-character pattern cap, `fuzzy`).
- `ocr`: `{engine, available, min_native_chars, modes, default}`. `available` is the honest answer — false both when CLASSIFIER_OCR_ENGINE=none and when the engine failed to load. Check it before blaming a failing text criterion on the document.
- `limits`: `max_pages` (CLASSIFIER_DOC_MAX_PAGES), `pdf_render_dpi`, `llm_text_char_budget`, and `images_per_llm_prompt` (1 — muse-glimmer runs without `--limit-mm-per-prompt`).

No request body. See API.md § `GET /document-kinds`.

formdata.description: The document to assess: JPEG, PNG, PDF, .txt, or .docx. The kind is detected from the bytes (common.documents.detect_kind), never from the filename or the part's Content-Type — a PDF uploaded as image/png still loads as a PDF, and a legacy .doc is rejected with a 400 telling you to convert it. Read into memory during the request via `await upload.read()`; the worker receives the bytes, so the UploadFile is not stored on disk. The `src` here points at a repo fixture — re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
Deprecated alias for `file`, still accepted so existing callers keep working. Send one of the two; `file` wins when both are present, and sending neither is a 400.

JSON array of CriterionInput objects. Each must have `name`; optional fields are `type` (`llm` default | `cv` | `text`), `weight` (float > 0, default 1.0), `hint` (`quality` | `presence` | `auto` default), and `depends_on` (name of another criterion that must PASS score >= 7 before this one runs — otherwise this criterion is marked SKIPPED and excluded from the weighted score). Chains are supported: A → B → C all skip if A fails.

type="text" adds `pattern` (defaults to `name`, max 500 chars), `match` (`contains` default | `exact` | `exact` is word/line anchored | `regex` | `fuzzy`), `case_sensitive` (false), `fuzzy_threshold` (0.85), and `min_count` (1). Text criteria are deterministic and cost no tokens; they search the document's native text layer, or the OCR'd text for a scan/photo. Use `fuzzy` on anything OCR'd. An empty, over-long, or invalid regex pattern is rejected with 400 at submit time.

If omitted, `config.DEFAULT_CRITERIA` is used.

Text-recognition policy: `auto` (default — recognise only when text is wanted and missing: a page carries an image whose native text is under CLASSIFIER_OCR_MIN_NATIVE_CHARS AND the request has a text or llm criterion), `always` (recognise every page image, replacing any native text), `never` (skip OCR; text criteria on an image-only document then score 1/FAIL with "No text available for this document…"). Anything else is a 400. A deployment with CLASSIFIER_OCR_ENGINE=none behaves as `never` regardless — check GET /document-kinds → `ocr.available`.

Where-did-you-find-it options. Absent (or `false`/`0`/`no`/`off`) = OFF, the default. `true` = regions + the SVG layer. A comma list (`svg,png,preview`) = regions + those layers. `none` = regions.json only, no pictures. Or the full object as a JSON string: `{"enabled": true, "layers": ["svg"], "layers_per_criterion": false, "llm_boxes": false, "detector": false}`. An unknown layer name is a **400 at submit time**, not a failed job. `regions.json` and `manifest.json` are always written when enabled, whatever `layers` says. See API.md § Regions and layers.

request.description:
Submit a single-document assessment job — JPEG, PNG, PDF, .txt, or .docx. Content-Type is `multipart/form-data`. Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{"job_id": "<id>", "phase": "pending"}` — this is the async pattern, so poll GET /jobs/{jobId} until `phase` is `completed` or `failed`, then read the `result` field.

Server-side flow (api/assess.py `assess_document`):
  1. Resolve the upload: the `file` part, or the legacy `image` alias; neither present is a 400.
  2. Validate the `ocr` mode and the declared content type (allowlist: image/jpeg, image/png, application/pdf, text/plain, the .docx type, application/octet-stream — the magic bytes have the final say).
  3. Parse the `criteria` JSON form field via `analysis.criteria.parse_criteria`, which also compiles any text pattern so a bad regex fails here rather than in a worker.
  4. Read the uploaded bytes into memory (UploadFile is only readable during the request).
  5. Create a job record in the SQLite jobs registry with `metadata={type: "assess", request_id: <req>}` and `initial_phase="staging"`.
  6. Write `{file_b64, content_type, filename, criteria, ocr}` to `PAYLOAD_DIR/<job_id>.json`, flip the row to `pending`, wake an idle worker (one of `CLASSIFIER_MAX_CONCURRENT`).
  7. Return `202` with the job_id.

The worker then loads the bytes into a Document (kind detection, PDF page rendering at CLASSIFIER_PDF_RENDER_DPI up to CLASSIFIER_DOC_MAX_PAGES, native text extraction), runs OCR if needed, then the cv / text / llm criteria.

Errors: **400** if no file was sent, the criteria list is empty, the body is empty, the `ocr` value is not auto|always|never, a text pattern is unusable, the content type is outside the allowlist, or the bytes are not a supported document (legacy .doc gets its own "convert to .docx" message); **422** if the criteria JSON fails Pydantic validation of CriterionInput.

Result shape once completed: `{image_info, document_info, assessment: {overall_verdict, overall_score, per_criterion_scores, weighted_score_breakdown}, verdict}`. `document_info` carries `kind`, `page_count`, `truncated_pages`, per-page `text_source`/`ocr_confidence`/`text_chars`, the `ocr` block (`mode`, `engine`, `ran`, `pages_recognised`), `text_sent_to_llm`, and `llm_image_page`. SKIPPED criteria appear in `per_criterion_scores` with `verdict: "SKIPPED"`, `score: null`, `method: "skipped"`, and a reason string, and are excluded from the weighted score — either because a `depends_on` did not pass, or because a `cv` criterion was sent against a .txt/.docx, which has no page images. See API.md § `POST /assess`.

Postman note: the `file` row's `src` points at a repo fixture (unit-tests/classifier/documents/invoice_native.pdf). Re-select the file if your working directory differs, and see the `Documents` folder for one ready-to-run request per fixture.

Regions: enable the `regions` form field to additionally collect WHERE each criterion found what it found and render the layers. The result then carries `page_geometry`, an `artifacts` block (files, urls, zip_url, total_bytes, expires_at, dropped, notes), and per-criterion `regions` / `regions_truncated` / `artifacts`. Nothing else about the response changes — the step is strictly additive and reads geometry off results the detectors already produced, so a score can never move because you asked where. See the `Regions` and `Artifacts` folders.

The field takes a shorthand (`true`, `svg,png,preview`, `none`, `false`) or the full JSON object, which is the only way to reach the two enrichments:

- `"detector": true` — hand the open-vocabulary detector (ai/detector) the cv criteria no OpenCV detector matches, and the localisation of llm presence criteria. Needs DETECTOR_URL.
- `"llm_boxes": true` — run the bounding-box enforcement loop for every `llm` criterion with hint presence/auto that the model scored 7 or higher: ask for a box on a 0-1000 grid, validate it (a full-frame box is rejected as a non-answer), crop it out of the ORIGINAL page and ask whether the feature is visible in the crop ALONE, and retry with the rejection as feedback, up to CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS. EVERY attempt comes back — in `localization.attempts` and as a region, rejected ones carrying `attrs.accepted: false` and reachable at `.../artifacts/p0.svg?criterion=<slug>&attempt=n`. It runs AFTER scoring and can never change a score or a verdict; assert that by submitting the same document with it off. Costs up to two small LLM calls per attempt per criterion.

`regions.diff` and `regions.examples` need a reference document, so on this endpoint they are recorded in the manifest and `artifacts.notes` says they were ignored. See API.md § The LLM enforcement loop.

Submit a comparison job — assess a subject document against one or more reference examples. Content-Type is `application/json`. Body is a CompareRequest (see api/schemas.py):

- `image`: DocumentInput `{data, type: "base64" | "url"}` — the field keeps its name for compatibility but accepts any supported kind (JPEG/PNG, PDF, .txt, .docx); the bytes decide, not the URL's extension. URL inputs are SSRF-checked before fetching (see analysis/loading.py). `ImageInput` remains an alias of `DocumentInput`.
- `criteria`: list[CriterionInput], defaults to `config.DEFAULT_CRITERIA` if omitted. `type: "text"` criteria work here exactly as on /assess.
- `aggregation`: `mean` (default, balanced) | `min` (strictest — must match all examples) | `max` (most lenient — must match any).
- `ocr`: `auto` (default) | `always` | `never`, applied to the subject AND every live example so their text layers are comparable.
- `examples`: list[ExampleInput] with `min_length=1`. Each has `data`, `type`, `weight` (0.0–1.0, default 0.5 — how much similarity to this example influences the combined score; `0.0` = ignore, `1.0` = similarity only), and optional `pre_generated_analysis` (a prior `result` from /assess to skip re-analysing the reference).

Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{"job_id": "<id>", "phase": "pending"}`. Poll GET /jobs/{jobId} for the result.

Server-side flow (api/assess.py `assess_with_reference`):
  1. Validate `request.criteria` non-empty (Pydantic already enforces `examples` min_length=1) and compile any text pattern, so a bad regex is a 400 here rather than a failed job.
  2. Create a job record with `metadata={type: "compare", request_id: <req>}` in phase `staging`.
  3. Write the full CompareRequest to `PAYLOAD_DIR/<job_id>.json`, flip the row to `pending`, wake an idle worker — jobs.runners.run_compare re-validates it from disk so the job survives a restart.
  4. Return `202` with the job_id.

Errors: **400** if criteria list is empty or a text pattern is unusable; **422** if the body fails CompareRequest validation (missing examples, invalid aggregation or ocr literal, weight out of range, malformed DocumentInput/ExampleInput).

Combined-score formula: `combined = (1 - weight) × input_overall_score + weight × similarity_score`. Result shape: `{status, criteria, aggregation, ocr, input_analysis, example_results[], aggregate: {method, combined_score, combined_verdict, per_example_combined_scores}}`; each analysis carries its own `document_info`. See API.md § `POST /assess/compare`.

Caching: `pre_generated_analysis` values must come from the SAME version of the classifier that is currently running — stored analyses from older versions cause runtime errors. Re-generate after upgrades. See API.md § Caching example analyses.

- `regions`: RegionsOptions or omitted (the default, off). Layers are rendered for the SUBJECT document unless `"examples": true`, which also collects regions and renders layers for each LIVE example as `e{i}.p{n}.<fmt>` in the same job directory (an example has no job of its own) plus its own `e{i}.regions.json`; off by default because it roughly doubles the artifact volume.
- `"diff": true` adds CHANGE DETECTION between the subject and each live single-image example: ORB features and a RANSAC homography align the two, then a thresholded difference yields `source: "diff"` polygons with `attrs.change` of added / removed / changed. They are filed under a synthetic `_diff:e{i}` criterion and rendered as `diff-e{i}-p0.<fmt>`. Under CLASSIFIER_DIFF_MIN_INLIERS (30) the answer is `aligned: false` with a note and NO regions — different framing is reported, not guessed at. Diff regions are NOT criteria: `aggregate`, every `similarity` and every `combined_score` are identical with `diff` on and off, which is the assertion worth making. An example supplied as `pre_generated_analysis` carries no pixels and is skipped with a reason. See the `Regions` folder's change-detection request and API.md § Change detection.

formdata.description: The document to search: JPEG, PNG, PDF, .txt, or .docx, same detection rules as /assess. The `src` here points at a repo fixture — re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
Deprecated alias for `file`, accepted for symmetry with /assess. Send one of the two.

JSON array of what to find. Entries are either BARE STRINGS or full CriterionInput objects, or a mix.

A bare string has no `type`, and defaulting it to `llm` would make the common case return nothing at all (LLM localization is phase 3). So it resolves to whichever path can actually produce geometry: `cv` when a registered OpenCV detector matches the name, else `detector` when DETECTOR_URL is configured (the open-vocabulary service can find anything nameable — `["bicycle"]` returns boxes with NO LLM call), else `llm`. The result's `method` field says which path each feature took.

An object spelled out in full is taken at its word — which is how a `text` feature sets `match`, `pattern`, `fuzzy_threshold`, and the rest, and how you force `"type": "detector"` for a name the OpenCV registry would otherwise fuzzy-match at difflib cutoff 0.6.

An empty array, a non-array, or an entry that fails CriterionInput validation is a 400.
Text-recognition policy, same three values as /assess. `always` here because the fixture is a PNG with no native text layer and the `Notice to Owner` feature needs OCR to have anything to locate.

Layer formats. `enabled` is IMPLIED on this endpoint — that is the point of it — so this field only chooses formats: `svg` (default), a comma list, `none` for regions.json only, or the full object as JSON. Sending `false` here does not disable regions; it is normalised back to enabled.

request.description:
Submit a scoring-free "where is X?" job. Same pipeline as /assess with every judgement taken out: no weighted score, no verdict, no dependency resolution, and no LLM call at all — unless the request sets `regions={"enabled":true,"llm_boxes":true}`, in which case a presence-only scoring call runs to give the bounding-box enforcement loop a score to gate on and its judgement is then discarded: the feature carries `regions` and `localization`, never a `score` or a `verdict`.

/assess answers "how good is this document?" and mentions, if asked, where it looked. /locate answers ONLY "where is X?", which is a different job with a different cost profile — a caller who wants boxes for a UI overlay should not have to submit criteria, read a verdict, and throw it away.

Returns **202 Accepted** immediately with `{"job_id": "<id>", "phase": "pending"}`; poll GET /jobs/{jobId}. `metadata.type` is `"locate"`, and the job uses the same job store, the same artifact directory layout, and the same artifact endpoints as an assess job.

**Result shape** (inside `job.result`): `features` where an assessment would have `assessment`, and no `verdict` anywhere. Each feature keeps `method`, `reason`, `detail`, `regions`, `regions_truncated` and `artifacts`, and loses `score`, `verdict` and `confidence` — "Green coverage: 14.2% of image" is a fact about where the thing is, not a verdict on it.

Feature resolution for a BARE STRING: `cv` when a registered OpenCV detector matches the name, else `detector` when DETECTOR_URL is set, else `llm` with `hint: "presence"` ("where is X" is a presence question by construction), which is what makes the enforcement loop eligible to run for it.

Errors: **400** for missing/unparseable `features`, an empty array, an invalid `ocr` value, an unknown `regions` layer, an empty file, or bytes that are not a supported document.

See API.md § `POST /locate`.

List recent jobs, newest first. Mounted by `common.jobs.router.build_router(jobs_registry, include_delete=True, include_cancel=False)` in main.py; backed by `SqliteRegistry.list_all()`. Returns a JobsListResponse — see `shared/common/src/common/jobs/model.py` for the JobBase shape. Result blobs are excluded from the list response (call GET /jobs/{job_id} to get the full `result` field).

Each job's `metadata` is the ClassifierMetadata blob `{type: "assess" | "compare", request_id: <req>}` written at submit time — useful for filtering by kind or correlating with the `[request_id]` in server logs (see middleware.py's CorrelationIDMiddleware). See API.md § `GET /jobs`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare.

request.description:
Poll for the status and result of a submitted job. Set the `jobId` collection variable to the `job_id` returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare first.

Response shape (JobBase from `common.jobs`):
  `{job_id, phase, created_at, updated_at, elapsed_seconds, metadata: {type, request_id}, result, error}`

`phase` progression: `staging` → `pending` → `processing` → `completed` | `failed`. Up to `CLASSIFIER_MAX_CONCURRENT` jobs sit in `processing` at once; a job left in `processing` by a restart is requeued to `pending` on the next startup.

- While `staging` / `pending` / `processing`: `result` is null, `error` is null. Keep polling.
- When `completed`: `result` is the assessment (see POST /assess or POST /assess/compare descriptions for the exact shape).
- When `failed`: `error` holds the exception message set by the worker via `jobs_registry.set_error(...)`, `result` is null.

Errors: **404** if the `job_id` is unknown (registry.get returned None). Note the response migration: top-level `id` is now `job_id`, `status` is now `phase`, and the previously separate `type` + `request_id` columns are nested under `metadata`. Callers that parse the response by field name need to update accordingly. See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess or POST /assess/compare.

request.description:
Delete a job record from the SQLite registry. Returns **204 No Content** on success (empty body). Idempotent from the caller's perspective in the sense that once gone the record stays gone — but the underlying `registry.delete` returns False for unknown ids, so a repeat call for the same id returns **404** with `detail: "no job '<id>'"`.

No cancel semantics: the worker doesn't currently observe a cancel signal mid-analysis, so `include_cancel=False` on the mounted router (see main.py). Deleting a job that's still `pending` removes the row before any worker claims it, so it never runs (its payload file is swept at the next startup). Deleting one that's `processing` does NOT abort the in-flight worker task — the worker will attempt to write its result/error to a row that no longer exists (logged, but harmless). See API.md § `DELETE /jobs/{job_id}`.

Also removes the job's artifact directory, via the `on_delete` hook `common.jobs.router.build_router` grew for exactly this — the router stays about job rows and the classifier plugs the directory cleanup in. To free the disk but KEEP the row and its inline regions, use DELETE /jobs/{jobId}/artifacts instead.

item.name: Documents
item.description:
One ready-to-run POST /assess per fixture in unit-tests/classifier/documents/ — a native PDF, a scanned PDF (with and without OCR), a .txt, a .docx, a well and a badly photographed letter, and a legacy .doc. Each request already carries criteria tailored to its fixture and states the expected outcome. Regenerate the fixtures with `uv run --package classifier python unit-tests/classifier/documents/make_fixtures.py`; the folder's README.md holds the same table plus curl equivalents.

Every request is async: the POST returns `{job_id, phase}`, so copy the job_id into the `jobId` collection variable and run GET /jobs/{jobId} to see the result. Postman resolves each `src` relative to its working directory — re-select the file if it cannot find it.

item.name: invoice_native.pdf — native text, all four match modes

formdata.description: 2-page PDF with a real text layer and a line-items table.

request.description:
Expected: overall PASS (~9). `Invoice #INV-2026-0042` PASS 10 (contains), `Notice to Owner` PASS 10 (fuzzy ratio ≈ 0.86 — the document says NOTICE TO OWNER), `Payment Terms: Net 30` PASS 10 on page 1 (`detail.pages` is `[1]`, i.e. the second page), `total amount` PASS 10 with `count: 3` (three dollar amounts), `lien waiver attached` FAIL 1 (best ratio ≈ 0.47, below the 0.5 partial-credit floor), `sharpness` PASS with `detail` ending "(worst of 2 pages — page N)", `document legibility` scored by the LLM from page 0's image plus the full text.

`document_info.ocr.ran` is **false**: a native text layer means ocr=auto never loads the models.

formdata.description: The same invoice as page IMAGES only — no text layer, 2° rotation, light noise.

request.description:
Expected: overall PASS (~9) with `document_info.ocr` = `{mode: "auto", engine: "rapidocr", ran: true, pages_recognised: 2}` and both pages reporting `text_source: "ocr"` at confidence ≈ 0.99.

All three text criteria PASS 10. Note `Invoice #INV-2026-0042` matches at ratio ≈ 0.98 rather than 1.0 — OCR drops the space in `Invoice#INV-…`, which is exactly why fuzzy is the right mode for recognised text. `contains` would have failed on that line.

item.name: invoice_scanned.pdf — same file with ocr=never (expect FAIL)

request.description:
The control for the previous request. Expected: `Notice to Owner` FAIL 1, confidence 0, `reason` = "No text available for this document (no native text layer and OCR did not run — ocr=never, or the OCR engine is disabled/unavailable). Re-submit with ocr=auto or always." `sharpness` still runs (it needs pixels, not text), and `document_info.ocr.ran` is false.

The fastest way to confirm OCR is what is doing the work in the ocr=auto run — and the same result you get from a deployment with CLASSIFIER_OCR_ENGINE=none.

formdata.description: Plain UTF-8 roofing agreement containing "Limited Warranty" and a date.

request.description:
Expected: overall PASS (~10). `Limited Warranty` PASS 10 with `count: 3` (heading plus two mentions in clause 2), `contract date` PASS 10 (regex matches 2026-03-14), `sharpness` **SKIPPED** — a .txt has no page images, so the criterion is not applicable and is excluded from the weighted score entirely (not FAIL, which would drag the document down for the wrong reason).

`document_info.llm_image_page` is `null`: the LLM prompt is text-only, and the system prompt tells the model to judge from the text. `ocr.ran` is false — no page images means nothing to recognise.

item.name: proposal.docx — paragraphs + table cells in document order

formdata.description: Headings, body paragraphs, and a specs table whose second row is System Size / 8.4 kW.

request.description:
Expected: overall PASS (~10). `Roofix Proposal` PASS 10 with `count: 2` (title plus the Terms paragraph). `System Size | 8.4 kW` PASS 10 — table rows are flattened to `cell | cell` during extraction, so a row is searchable as one line; this is the criterion to copy when checking a spec table. `has faces` **SKIPPED** (no page images). `states the system size` is scored by the LLM from a text-only prompt.

Paragraphs and table cells arrive in document order (the body XML is walked, not python-docx's separate `paragraphs` / `tables` lists), so a table between two headings stays between them.

formdata.description: A letter photographed at ~3° skew with an uneven brightness gradient, mild blur, and JPEG noise.

request.description:
Expected: overall PASS (~10). OCR recognises the page (`text_source: "ocr"`, confidence ≈ 0.99), so `Notice to Owner` PASSes at ratio ≈ 0.88 and `case number` PASSes on CASE-77813. `sharpness` PASS (Laplacian variance ≈ 330 against a threshold of 100) and `proper exposure` PASS (mean ≈ 203 — the gradient stays inside the accepted band).

This is the everyday field case: a photo of paper that a `text` criterion can still be trusted on.

formdata.description: The same letter, heavily out of focus.

request.description:
Expected: overall MARGINAL (~5). `sharpness` FAIL 1 (Laplacian variance ≈ 6). OCR only manages the two large headings (~32 characters), so `Notice to Owner` still PASSes while `case number` FAILs 1 — body text is gone. `document legibility` is **SKIPPED** because its `depends_on: sharpness` did not PASS, which means the LLM is never called at all for this document.

The pattern worth copying: gate expensive llm criteria behind a cheap `cv` quality check so an unusable photo costs no tokens.

formdata.description: 64 bytes starting with the OLE2 magic D0 CF 11 E0 A1 B1 1A E1.

request.description:
Expected: **400 Bad Request**, no job created, with `detail` = "Legacy .doc (OLE2 compound) files are not supported. Convert the file to .docx (Word: File → Save As → .docx, or `libreoffice --convert-to docx`) and upload that instead."

Detection is by magic bytes, so renaming the file to .docx does not change the outcome — and neither does declaring a different Content-Type. There is no server-side conversion step by design; converting is the caller's job.

item.name: Artifacts
item.description:
The per-job artifact directory: the manifest, one file at a time (optionally re-rendered for a subset of regions), the whole thing as a zip, and an early delete.

All four live in the classifier (ai/classifier/api/artifacts.py), not in `common.jobs.router` — the router stays about job rows. They share the Authorization posture of every other route: the LiteLLM pass-through does the bearer check, and direct :8005 access is unauthenticated.

Every request needs a `jobId` from a job submitted WITH `regions` (or any /locate job). A job that never had artifacts answers **404**; one whose directory the sweeper or a DELETE removed answers **410**, so a caller holding a stored URL can tell "expired" from "wrong URL" without guessing.

Binary streaming through the LiteLLM pass-through is the one thing worth verifying on a new deployment — if a PNG or a zip arrives corrupted, fall back to direct :${PORT_CLASSIFIER} for layer downloads and say so in your runbook.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess, POST /assess/compare, or POST /locate. The job must have been submitted WITH `regions`, or it has no artifact directory and these endpoints answer 404.

request.description:
The manifest for a job's artifact directory: `files[]` (name, bytes, content type, url), the criterion → slug map, `page_geometry`, the request's `regions` options, `dropped`, `notes`, `total_bytes`, and `expires_at`.

The same information as the result's `artifacts` block, fetchable WITHOUT pulling the (possibly large) result — which is the point: a caller that only wants to list the layers should not drag a megabyte of regions through the job store to do it.

**Errors:** 404 when the job is unknown or never had artifacts (submitted without `regions`); 410 when the job exists and its result says it DID have artifacts but the directory is gone — swept past JOB_TTL_HOURS, or explicitly deleted.

See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts`.

variable.description: job_id of a job submitted with `regions`.

File name from GET /jobs/{jobId}/artifacts. Three families live in one directory: the SUBJECT's own `regions.json`, `manifest.json`, `p0.svg`, `p0.layer.png`, `p0.preview.jpg`, `p0.base.jpg`; change-detection layers `diff-e0-p0.svg` etc. from `regions.diff` on /assess/compare; and, from `regions.examples`, an example's own `e0.p0.svg` plus its `e0.regions.json` (an example's pages are a different coordinate frame, so it gets its own regions file rather than being mixed into the subject's). Validated against a strict pattern AND against the directory, so no path traversal and no listing the volume.

query.description: Criterion SLUG (not name) — e.g. `has-water-4b21`, from the manifest's criteria map. Repeatable. Filters the re-render to that criterion's regions. An unknown slug is a 400.
Comma list of `cv`, `ocr`, `pdf-text`, `llm`, `detector`, `diff`. Only regions from those sources are drawn.

LLM criteria only: the box from enforcement-loop attempt N, accepted or not. This is how a REJECTED box is viewed on its own — the loop stores every attempt, and `artifacts.attempts[]` in the job result carries these URLs ready-made. Non-LLM regions have no attempt and are dropped by this filter, which is what "show me attempt 2" means.

LLM criteria only, tri-state. `true` — and the DEFAULT whenever any filter is given and no `attempt` is — keeps the accepted attempt, which is the same subset the stored combined layer shows. `false` keeps the REJECTED attempts, for looking at what the loop threw away.

request.description:
Stream one file with its content type (`image/svg+xml`, `image/png`, `image/jpeg`, `application/json`).

With NO query parameters the stored file is streamed as-is. With any of them the layer is **re-rendered from regions.json** by the same `common.vision.render_*` functions that produced the stored one, so a filtered view is always consistent with the combined one.

SVG renders are cheap enough to serve uncached. A filtered PNG or preview for a SINGLE criterion is cached into the directory as `p0.<slug>.layer.png` / `p0.<slug>.preview.jpg` on first request — the same names `regions.layers_per_criterion` pre-renders, so the lazy and eager paths cannot produce different files — and counts against CLASSIFIER_ARTIFACT_MAX_BYTES.

**Errors:** 400 for an unknown criterion slug or a name that is not a renderable layer (you cannot filter manifest.json); 404 for an unknown job or a file not in the directory; 410 when the directory has been swept or deleted. A filtered `preview` needs `p{n}.base.jpg`, which exists only when the job asked for the `preview` layer — without it the response is a 404 that says so and points at the SVG or PNG instead.

See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts/{name}`.

All three layer families take these filters. `diff-e0-p0.svg` renders from the subject's `regions.json` (the diff is in the subject's coordinate frame and is filed there under `_diff:e0`); `e0.p0.svg` renders from `e0.regions.json`. A `?attempt=` or `?accepted=false` render is deliberately UNcached — it is an inspection, not a hot path, and caching it under the criterion's name would serve the wrong subset to the next caller who asked for the plain one.

variable.description: job_id of a job submitted with `regions`.

request.description:
Every file in the directory as one zip, built on the fly and streamed — nothing extra is stored. The "download the layers" path, for Photoshop or a report generator.

Entries are prefixed with the job id, so unpacking several jobs side by side does not collide. Built from the files that are ACTUALLY there, so a job the byte cap trimmed produces a zip of what survived rather than failing.

In Postman use Send → Save Response → Save to a file; the preview pane cannot show a zip.

**Errors:** 404 unknown job or no directory; 410 swept or deleted.

See API.md § `GET /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts.zip`.

variable.description: job_id returned by POST /assess, POST /assess/compare, or POST /locate. The job must have been submitted WITH `regions`, or it has no artifact directory and these endpoints answer 404.

request.description:
Remove the artifact directory but KEEP the job row and its result — the inline regions (up to CLASSIFIER_INLINE_REGIONS_MAX) survive. For a caller that copied the layers elsewhere and wants the disk back before the TTL.

Returns **204 No Content**. Afterwards the other three artifact endpoints answer **410** for this job, not 404: the job still says it had artifacts, they are simply gone.

**Errors:** 404 when the job is unknown or has no directory.

To delete the row as well, use DELETE /jobs/{jobId}, which removes both.

See API.md § `DELETE /jobs/{job_id}/artifacts`.

item.name: Regions
item.description:
One ready-to-run request per fixture in unit-tests/classifier/regions/, mirroring that folder's README — which lists the exact regions each one should produce, down to approximate bounding boxes. Run one, copy its `job_id` into the `jobId` variable, then use the `Artifacts` folder to fetch the layers.

The `cv` and `text` rows are deterministic and should reproduce exactly. Anything `llm` does not localise in this build at all (phase 3) and comes back with `"regions": []` and `"artifacts": null` — no regions must mean a NULL artifacts block, never an empty object implying URLs that would 404.

item.name: greenery_and_sky.png — three mask detectors, three polygon sets

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/regions/greenery_and_sky.png. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
See the request description for what each entry is expected to localise.
Text-recognition policy for this fixture.
Layer formats for this run — see API.md § Regions and layers for the full option set.

request.description:
Three HSV mask detectors on one 900×700 synthetic scene, plus a whole-page measurement that must produce NOTHING.

**Expect:** `has sky` PASS 10, 1 polygon bounded by roughly (0, 0, 899, 243) — the detector only looks at the top 35% of the page, so the polygon is that band. `has vegetation` PASS 10, 1 polygon around (0, 359, 899, 699) with ~8 vertices after approxPolyDP. `has water` PASS 10 with **2** polygons: the sky band AND the pool at ~(90, 518, 430, 651) — expected and worth understanding, because `detect_water` accepts any blue region whose Laplacian variance is under 200 and a smooth sky qualifies. That is the detector's honest answer, not a fixture flaw.

`sharpness` PASSes with `"regions": []` and `"artifacts": null`: a whole-page measurement never fabricates a full-page box.

Artifacts written: manifest.json, regions.json, p0.svg, p0.layer.png, p0.preview.jpg, and p0.base.jpg — the un-annotated page, kept only because `preview` was requested, so a FILTERED preview can be re-composited later (a burned-in preview cannot be un-burned).

item.name: text_blocks.png — merged text-block boxes + OCR line polygons

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/regions/text_blocks.png. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
See the request description for what each entry is expected to localise.
Text-recognition policy for this fixture.
Layer formats for this run — see API.md § Regions and layers for the full option set.

request.description:
Two sources on one page: `cv` block boxes and `ocr` line polygons. `ocr=always` because a PNG has no native text layer, so the text criteria have nothing to search otherwise.

**Expect:** `has text` MARGINAL 5 with **4** boxes, one per paragraph cluster — roughly (96,192)-(352,288), (512,192)-(768,256), (512,448)-(800,480) and (96,416)-(256,480). Two columns producing more than one box is the point of this fixture: a single box over the whole page would mean the 32×32 block merge is broken.

`Notice to Owner` PASS 10 with 1—2 polygons, `source: "ocr"`, carrying the recogniser's confidence as `score` — a fuzzy window can clip the line above, so two regions is normal. `total amount` PASS 10, 1 `ocr` polygon on the `$4,850.00` line.

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/documents/invoice_native.pdf. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
See the request description for what each entry is expected to localise.
Text-recognition policy for this fixture.
Layer formats for this run — see API.md § Regions and layers for the full option set.

request.description:
PyMuPDF rectangles instead of OCR polygons. `ocr=never` because the PDF has a native text layer — that is what makes the source `pdf-text`.

**Expect:** `Notice to Owner` 1 box located by `search_for`, with `attrs.pdf_rect` ≈ [60.0, 220.2, 193.8, 239.4] — the region's own `points` are in RENDERED page pixels (1240×1755 at 150 dpi) and `pdf_rect` is the same rectangle in POINTS, so PDF tooling can use it directly.

`total amount` 3 boxes ($1,200.00, $3,650.00, $4,850.00), each reconstructed from the word spans covering the regex match — **approximate by construction**: a phrase PyMuPDF splits differently from the text layer (hyphenation, a ligature, a column break mid-phrase) does not line up, and the region is omitted rather than guessed at.

`has text` produces boxes on BOTH pages even though the score reports the worst one — "where is the text" is a different question from "how much of it is there".

`page_geometry[0].pdf_points` is [595.2, 842.4] and `working_scale` ≈ 0.569.

item.name: Neighborhood.jpeg — a real photo, and the empty-regions case

request.description:
The only honest input for `has faces`: a real street photo. A drawn face does not reliably trip OpenCV's Haar cascade — it was trained on photographs — so there is deliberately no synthetic face fixture.

**Expect:** `has sky` PASS with ~3 polygons. `has faces` usually finds NOTHING on this photo (the people are small and not frontal), in which case it FAILs with `"regions": []` and `"artifacts": null` — which is the assertion worth making: no regions must mean a null artifacts block, never an empty object implying URLs that would 404.

item.name: Neighborhood.jpeg — regions.detector, scored with no LLM call

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/Neighborhood.jpeg. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
See the request description for what each entry is expected to localise.
formdata.value: [{"name":"has roof vent","type":"cv"},{"name":"has bicycle","type":"detector"},{"name":"has sky","type":"cv"},{"name":"has solar panels","type":"llm","hint":"presence"}]

formdata.description: Text-recognition policy for this fixture.
Layer formats for this run — see API.md § Regions and layers for the full option set.

request.description:
Phase 2: the open-vocabulary detector (ai/detector) answering the criteria OpenCV cannot.

**Needs DETECTOR_URL set on the classifier container** (`http://detector:8000`). Without it the job still SUCCEEDS — an unreachable enrichment never fails a job — and `result.artifacts.notes` says the service is not configured, which is the other assertion worth making here. Check GET /document-kinds → `regions.detector.configured` first.

Four criteria, four paths. `has roof vent` is a `cv` criterion NO OpenCV detector matches, so with `regions.detector` on it is answered by the detector and SCORED from the boxes. `has bicycle` spells `"type": "detector"` to name the path outright; as a `cv` criterion it would also reach the service now that `get_detector`'s fuzzy cutoff is 0.8 (`CV_NAME_FUZZY_CUTOFF`) rather than the 0.6 that used to collide it with `has faces`. `has sky` has a real OpenCV detector and is untouched. `has solar panels` is LLM-scored but detector-LOCALISED.

**Expect:** `has roof vent` and `has bicycle` with `"method": "detector"`, `source="detector"` regions carrying `attrs.detector_score`, and a score of 10 (best box ≥ 0.5) or 7 (above the 0.25 floor) — or 1/FAIL if the detector genuinely finds neither, which on this photo is the likely answer and is still the right assertion: a detector negative is FAILed there and is NOT then re-asked of the vision model, because that would charge a token cost for every absent feature.

`has sky` still reports `"method": "cv"`. `has solar panels` still reports `"method": "llm"` — the model scores it, the detector only says where — so its regions (if any) have `source="detector"`.

`result.document_info.detector` reports the model, device, call count and inference time; regions.json carries the same block at the top so a consumer can tell which model drew the boxes. One detector call is made per page image, carrying every label for that page.

See API.md § The detector and ai/detector/DETECTOR.md.

item.name: POST /locate — text_blocks.png, no score, just the geometry

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/regions/text_blocks.png. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
See the request description for what each entry is expected to localise.
Text-recognition policy for this fixture.
Layer formats for this run — see API.md § Regions and layers for the full option set.

request.description:
The same fixture through /locate instead of /assess. Note the field is `features`, not `criteria`, and that entries may be bare names or full objects.

**Expect:** `result.features` with the same regions as the /assess run above, and NO `assessment`, `verdict`, `overall_score` or per-feature `score`/`confidence` anywhere. `metadata.type` is `"locate"`.

Add a feature no OpenCV detector resolves (e.g. `"bicycle"`): with DETECTOR_URL set it comes back with `"method": "detector"` and real boxes and NO LLM call, and without it with `regions: []` and a reason saying LLM localization is phase 3.

formdata.description: Repo fixture: unit-tests/classifier/Neighborhood.jpeg. Re-select the file in Postman if your working directory differs.
Two presence criteria the model can plausibly box, and one quality criterion the loop must IGNORE.
Text-recognition policy for this fixture.
The full object — `llm_boxes` and `detector` are not layer formats, so the comma shorthand cannot express them.

request.description:
Phase 3: the vision model draws a box, and then has to prove it.

For each `llm` criterion with hint presence/auto that the scoring call scored 7 or higher, the classifier runs a separate loop: **ask** for `[x1,y1,x2,y2]` on a 0-1000 grid of the same page image → **validate** (four numbers, x1<x2, y1<y2, inside the grid, area between 0.2% and 95% — a full-frame box is a refusal dressed as an answer and is the commonest failure) → **verify** by cropping that box out of the ORIGINAL page, padding it 10%, and sending the CROP ALONE with "is <criterion> visible in this? 1-10" → **retry** with the rejection as feedback, up to CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_MAX_ATTEMPTS (3).

**Expect** `per_criterion_scores["solar panels"].localization` with `attempts` (one entry per round: `bbox_grid`, `bbox_px`, `valid`, `reject`, `verify_score`, `verify_reason`, `accepted`), `accepted_attempt` (or `null` when nothing was accepted), and `calls`. `regions` carries EVERY attempt that produced four numbers — the accepted one first, the rejected ones with `attrs.accepted: false`.

**`image sharpness` must have NO attempts at all.** It is a property of the whole page; boxing it would be a fabrication, and the gate skips hint=quality criteria entirely.

**With `"detector": true` as well** (needs DETECTOR_URL), each accepted box also carries `attrs.detector_iou` — its overlap with the open-vocabulary detector's best box for the same label. Informational only: it never accepts or rejects. Under ~0.5 the two sources disagree about what the criterion means, which is a wording problem, not a geometry one.

**Viewing a REJECTED box** is the point of returning all of them:
```
GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts/p0.svg?criterion=<slug>&attempt=1
GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts/p0.preview.jpg?criterion=<slug>&attempt=1
```
with no `attempt`, `?criterion=<slug>` renders the ACCEPTED box only — the same subset the stored combined `p0.svg` shows. `artifacts.attempts[]` in the result carries those URLs ready-made.

**The assertion worth making:** send the same request with `"llm_boxes": false` and compare every `score` and `verdict`. They must be identical. The loop runs AFTER scoring and only adds keys — including in the case where every attempt was rejected.

**Cost:** one ask per attempt plus one verify per attempt whose box validated, each capped at CLASSIFIER_LLM_BBOX_MAX_TOKENS (1024, most of which is reasoning). Run `bin/grounding_experiment.py` on the box for the real hit rate on your model before relying on it.

See API.md § The LLM enforcement loop.

Phase 4: change detection between two photographs of the same scene.

**Fill the two collection variables first.** This endpoint takes JSON, not multipart, so the images have to be base64 in the body — and ~300 KB of base64 inlined in a collection file is unreadable and unmergeable. So the body references `{{scene_after_b64}}` (the SUBJECT) and `{{scene_before_b64}}` (the reference EXAMPLE), and you paste the encoded fixtures into the collection variables once:

```bash
# Linux
base64 -w0 unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_before.png
base64 -w0 unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_after.png
# macOS
base64 -i unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_before.png | tr -d '\n'
# PowerShell
[Convert]::ToBase64String([IO.File]::ReadAllBytes('unit-tests/classifier/regions/scene_before.png'))
```

Postman → the collection → Variables → paste into CURRENT VALUE for `scene_before_b64` and `scene_after_b64`. (Both files are generated by `unit-tests/classifier/regions/make_fixtures.py`; if you would rather host them, swap each object to `{"data": "https://...", "type": "url"}` — URL inputs are SSRF-checked before fetching.)

**The fixtures.** One synthetic yard photographed twice: the camera moved ~6 px and rotated ~1°, a red car appeared, and a shed went. The shift is deliberate — two pixel-aligned images would let a diff that never aligns anything look correct.

**Expect** `result.example_results[0].diff` with `aligned: true`, `inliers` around 147, `changes: {added: 1, removed: 2, changed: 0}`, and polygons carrying `source: "diff"` and `attrs.change`. The added region sits at roughly (130, 509)-(340, 623) — the car; the removed ones at roughly (704, 322)-(837, 362) and (754, 423)-(790, 471) — the shed's roofline and its door (a flat wall against flat ground does not clear the Otsu threshold in the middle, so it fragments; two regions in the right place is the honest output).

**The house must NOT be a region.** It is in both frames; if it shows up, the homography was not applied.

**Files written** (GET /jobs/:jobId/artifacts): `diff-e0-p0.svg` and `diff-e0-p0.preview.jpg` for the change layer, `e0.p0.svg` and `e0.regions.json` from `"examples": true`, alongside the subject's own `p0.*`. All three families take the `?criterion=` / `?source=` filters.

**The assertion worth making:** send the same body with `"diff": false` and compare `result.aggregate`. It must be identical. Diff regions are not criteria — they never reach the weighted score or the similarity comparison.

**Negative check:** swap `scene_before_b64` for any unrelated image and the answer must be `aligned: false` with `regions: []` and a note saying the two are probably not views of the same scene — not a page full of boxes.

See API.md § Change detection and unit-tests/classifier/regions/README.md.
